text: For each requested page, write one row in `workspace/plan.md`: Reader / decision | Selected evidence and limits | Central product mechanism | Opening message | Decision material visible on page | Section sequence | Visual emphasis / source ancestors | Actual next action

For argument alternatives, give each page a useful reason to exist: an operator understanding a workflow, an evaluator inspecting fit, or a sponsor considering the scope of an evaluation. These are possible decisions, not assumed buying roles.
For layout-only alternatives, preserve the approved proposition and supplied copy. … Change copy only where the user allows it; do not force a new argument into a visual comparison.

each page must still explain the product and provide enough relevant material to support its reader's decision. Shortening one sibling or adding a salutation does not create a different useful argument.

loc: Make the visual difference serve the decision
text: Three centered heroes followed by the same product screenshot and gradient closer are still one composition, even with different headlines or fewer sections. Section shuffling, recoloring or new card icons alone do not establish a new direction.

loc: Write and review as a set
text: When the request includes argument alternatives, different headlines should express different useful arguments, not three synonyms for the same promise.

loc: Write and review as a set
text: At review, compare the actual rendered siblings with the direction rows. … If only one page is finished, report one finished page.
